stages.description: Audit demonstrable skills, research industry verticals, analyze competing providers, and define a credible agency positioning statement.
Productize bespoke services into 3 tiered packages (Entry, Core, Extended) with defined deliverables, boundaries, and revision limits.
Calculate direct delivery labor, software costs, utilization rate, overhead absorption, gross margin, and operating profit.
Evaluate inbound and outbound opportunities against an Ideal Client Profile, budget constraints, timeline, and delivery feasibility.
Conduct structured discovery calls, present transparent proposals, manage deal stages in CRM, and execute formal service agreements.
Execute a multi-point client onboarding checklist, secure credentials, host kickoff meetings, and configure project workspaces.
Break down scope into sprint tasks, assign contractor responsibilities via RACI, and track milestone execution against deadlines.
Conduct internal quality assurance checks, enforce acceptance criteria, manage revisions, and secure client sign-off.
Issue compliant tax invoices, track payment milestones, reconcile accounts receivable, and manage working capital.
Review service performance metrics, gather client feedback, address retention opportunities, and update operational SOPs.

why_now.industry_shift: Modern clients increasingly reject bloated legacy agencies with high overheads and unpredictable solo freelancers in favor of structured, specialized boutique agencies with transparent pricing, clear SLAs, and rigorous operational accountability.
why_now.ai_impact: Responsible AI accelerates research, documentation, meeting transcription, and initial drafting—allowing small, well-organized agencies to operate with high operational clarity while maintaining mandatory human review for quality, accuracy, and compliance.
why_now.business_demand: Mid-market companies and growing brands require reliable service delivery partners who combine technical excellence with documented processes, reliable communication cadences, and professional risk management.
why_now.economic_reality: Building an agency requires operational discipline and financial literacy: distinguishing revenue from profit, profit from cash flow, and understanding that capacity and delivery costs dictate sustainable growth.

agency_economics_2027.heading: Build a Lean Agency With Real Financial and Operational Control.
agency_economics_2027.approved_copy: Learn the financial and operational realities of a small service agency. Evaluate service costs, capacity, contractor responsibilities, overhead, sales uncertainty and cash flow before making growth decisions. Build systems that support consistent delivery without relying on unrealistic revenue or automation promises.

corrections.title: Lean Does Not Mean Zero Overhead
corrections.explanation: Every functioning agency incurs ongoing operational expenses: project management and CRM software subscriptions, accounting fees, tax compliance, marketing assets, hardware, backup systems, security tools, sales time, and founder administration.

corrections.title: Contractors Do Not Eliminate Management
corrections.explanation: Working with specialist contractors requires rigorous role specifications, clear task briefs, paid sample evaluations, onboarding workflows, quality control, communication coordination, timely compensation, access control, and confidentiality oversight.

corrections.title: Retainers Do Not Guarantee Stability
corrections.explanation: Retainer contracts carry distinct commercial risks including sudden client cancellation, underpriced scope creep, excessive over-servicing, delayed invoice payments, client concentration vulnerability, and unpredictable monthly churn.

corrections.title: Automation Does Not Remove Responsibility
corrections.explanation: Automated pipelines and AI drafting tools require active human oversight, client confidentiality protection, factual validation, exception handling, system monitoring, and transparent client communication.

corrections.title: Growth Must Match Capacity
corrections.explanation: Sustainable agency expansion requires balancing client acquisition with actual delivery capacity, founder supervisory hours, contractor availability, direct delivery costs, QA thoroughness, and sufficient working capital.

india_compliance_awareness.heading: Understand the Business Responsibilities Behind Agency Ownership in India.
india_compliance_awareness.educational_nature: This curriculum provides educational awareness of general agency business, financial, and compliance responsibilities. It does not constitute formal legal, taxation, or accounting advice.
india_compliance_awareness.disclaimer: The course provides general awareness of agency business, financial and compliance responsibilities. Registration, tax, contracts, intellectual property, data protection and cross-border payment obligations depend on individual circumstances and applicable law. Consult qualified professionals before taking legal, financial or regulatory action.

topics.concepts: Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Limited Liability Partnership (LLP), and Private Limited Company models; personal liability distinctions, registration considerations, statutory filings, and professional consultation with a practicing Chartered Accountant or Company Secretary.

Understanding what MSME / Udyam registration is, micro and small enterprise classification benchmarks, official government portal procedures (udyamregistration.gov.in), free registration awareness, and distinguishing Udyam from mandatory corporate incorporation or GST registration.

Goods and Services Tax (GST) threshold applicability for service providers, registered vs unregistered operations, mandatory invoice fields under CBIC GST Invoice Rules, tax invoices vs bills of supply, export-of-services principles, recordkeeping, and monthly/quarterly return awareness verified by an accountant.

Master Service Agreements (MSA), Statements of Work (SOW), scope definitions, milestone payment schedules, intellectual property transfer conditions, confidentiality (NDA) clauses, limitation of liability, termination provisions, and dispute resolution mechanisms.

Copyright ownership principles, trademark awareness, stock asset licensing compliance, custom client deliverable assignment, contractor work-for-hire agreements, font licensing, and avoidance of IP infringement.

Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 and DPDP Rules, 2025; phased commencement awareness, client and prospective customer personal data handling, CRM contact consent, data minimization, access control, secure storage, and confidentiality boundaries.

Authorized dealer bank remittances, cross-border payment processors, Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) awareness, Foreign Inward Remittance Certificates / Advice (FIRC/FIRA), currency conversion fees, and export-of-services documentation requirements.

portfolio.title: Digital Agency Operations Blueprint — Business, Finance, Sales & Delivery
portfolio.description: One unified, comprehensive operational capstone demonstrating the business, financial, sales, delivery, and governance architecture required to launch and operate a small digital service agency.

components.title: Component 01 — Agency Niche & Positioning
deliverables: Simulated agency brand identity and core mission statement
Selected industry vertical and specific buyer persona profile
Demonstrable service capability audit and portfolio evidence log
Competitive matrix comparing 3 competing agencies with market differentiation rationale
Credible agency positioning statement avoiding exaggerated claims
Initial business model assumptions and delivery risk register

components.title: Component 02 — Three Service Packages
deliverables: Entry Package: Fixed-scope initial assessment or starter engagement with defined deliverables, 7-10 day turnaround, and strict revision bounds
Core Package: Primary high-value flagship service offering with multi-stage milestones, client dependencies, and targeted gross margin
Extended Package: Comprehensive retainer or expanded delivery scope with SLA turnarounds, ongoing optimization, and dedicated capacity allocation
Detailed specification for all 3 packages: target buyer, problem solved, deliverables, schedule, exclusions, pricing, direct delivery costs, gross margin, and monthly capacity constraints

components.title: Component 03 — Pricing & Profitability Model
deliverables: Structured Google Sheets model with documented assumptions and formula integrity (no divide-by-zero or circular references)
Direct service costing breakdown distinguishing labor hours, contractor fees, and project-specific software
Billable utilization calculator: Billable Hours ÷ Available Work Hours × 100
Gross margin schedule: Gross Profit (Revenue - Direct Costs) ÷ Revenue × 100
Operating overhead schedule allocating software licenses, accounting, marketing, and founder admin time
Operating profit calculation: Revenue - Direct Costs - Operating Expenses
3-Scenario Cash-Flow Forecast: Conservative (loss-making stress test), Base (realistic ramp), and Optimistic (capacity ceiling)
Client concentration risk metric: Revenue from Single Client ÷ Total Revenue × 100

components.title: Component 04 — CRM Sales Pipeline
deliverables: Configured 7-stage pipeline: New Lead → Qualification → Discovery → Proposal → Clarification/Decision → Won → Lost
Documented stage exit criteria and conversion probability percentages
Simulated prospect records populated with deal values, decision-maker contacts, pain points, next action dates, and qualification notes
Sales handoff protocol transferring confirmed scope, client assets, and commercial terms to delivery operations

components.title: Component 05 — Client Onboarding Checklist
deliverables: 12-point structured onboarding protocol covering sales-to-delivery handoff and commercial contract verification
Client asset intake form, brand guideline requests, and stakeholder contact directory
Secure credential access protocol and permission provisioning checklist
Kickoff meeting agenda template with expectation alignment and milestone confirmation
Client communication SLA agreement: communication channels, weekly update cadence, and escalation paths
Shared project workspace setup and client portal directory organization

components.title: Component 06 — Five Core Operational SOPs
deliverables: SOP 01: Lead Qualification & CRM Handoff (Trigger, BANT criteria, deal stage progression, and proposal readiness check)
SOP 02: Client Onboarding & Secure Access (Welcome package, credential collection via password manager, and kickoff scheduling)
SOP 03: Project Execution & Quality Assurance (Sprint task allocation, milestone tracking, peer QA gate, and pre-delivery sign-off)
SOP 04: Feedback, Revisions & Scope Changes (Client review intake, revision round tracking, out-of-scope change order pricing and authorization)
SOP 05: Reporting, Delivery & Offboarding (Final deliverable transfer, asset archive, client acceptance sign-off, post-launch feedback, and retention review)
Standardized format for each SOP: Title, Purpose, Trigger, Owner, Inputs, Tools, Step-by-Step Actions, Approval Roles, Outputs, QA Checklist, Exceptions, Escalation, Version Date

components.title: Component 07 — Contractor Evaluation Kit
deliverables: Detailed role specification for a specialized delivery contractor (skills, portfolio requirements, availability, and toolchain)
Paid sample assessment task brief with realistic deliverables, turnaround deadline, and fair test compensation assumptions
Candidate scoring rubric evaluating technical quality, communication speed, brief adherence, and revision responsiveness
Comparative evaluation of 2 fictional/anonymized contractor profiles with objective selection rationale
Contractor onboarding checklist covering project workspace access, SOP orientation, and task management standards
Access control, data protection, and confidentiality oversight checklist
Legal review checklist outlining required clauses for independent contractor agreements (IP assignment, confidentiality, non-solicitation)

components.title: Component 08 — 90-Day Agency Action Plan
deliverables: Phase 1 (Days 01–30) — Validate & Prepare: Skill audit, niche research, positioning statement, 3 service packages, financial model assumptions, compliance research, and operating document drafts
Phase 2 (Days 31–60) — Build & Simulate: CRM pipeline setup, proposal templates, delivery project board, 5 operational SOPs, contractor evaluation simulation, and quality assurance testing

Phase 3 (Days 61–90) — Review & Launch Readiness: Pricing refinement, cash-flow stress testing, acquisition channel evaluation, capacity validation, governance review, blueprint presentation, and professional consultation readiness
Documented action plan table with Activity, Owner, Start/End Window, Deliverable, Resource Needs, Estimated Cost, Dependency, Risk, Quality Measure, and Decision Points

simulated_workflow.title: 10-Stage Simulated Agency Service Delivery
simulated_workflow.description: A single, coherent fictional client scenario executed through all operational stages from lead to retention review:
stages: Stage 01: Lead Identified — Inbound enquiry recorded in CRM with initial qualification notes
Stage 02: Discovery — Structured discovery meeting assessing business goals, budget, timeline, and scope
Stage 03: Service Selection — Mapping client need to Core Package with agreed customization parameters
Stage 04: Proposal & Contract — Tailored proposal presented with scope of work, milestone pricing, and payment terms
Stage 05: Client Onboarding — Onboarding checklist executed, assets collected, kickoff held, and project board launched
Stage 06: Delivery Execution — Sprint tasks assigned, contractor task simulated, and weekly status report delivered
Stage 07: Quality Assurance — Internal QA gate passed against acceptance criteria and brand specifications
Stage 08: Client Handover — Deliverables presented, revision round processed, and final sign-off secured
Stage 09: Invoicing & Reporting — Tax invoice issued, payment reconciliation noted, and project closure report filed
Stage 10: Retention Review — Client satisfaction review conducted, performance evaluated, and retainer renewal explored

faq.question: What is this course about?
faq.answer: It teaches the practical business, financial, sales, delivery and management systems used to plan and operate a small digital or creative service agency.

faq.question: Who should join?
faq.answer: Skilled freelancers, consultants, digital service professionals and small business operators who want more structured service delivery.

faq.question: Do I need an existing agency?
faq.answer: No. You may complete the course through a simulated agency model.

faq.question: Do I need a fixed monthly freelance income?
faq.answer: No. Demonstrable service skills or relevant project experience are sufficient for the stated prerequisite.

faq.question: What is the course duration?
faq.answer: Eight weeks with 64 guided training hours.

faq.question: What is the course fee?
faq.answer: ₹12,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified pricing and tax policy.

faq.question: Will I learn niche and service selection?
faq.answer: Yes. You will evaluate markets, buyers, competition and agency positioning.

faq.question: Will I create service packages?
faq.answer: Yes. You will design three packages with deliverables, pricing, scope and delivery assumptions.

faq.question: Will I learn agency pricing and finances?
faq.answer: Yes. The course includes delivery cost, utilization, overhead, margins, revenue scenarios and cash-flow fundamentals.

faq.question: Does the course teach HubSpot CRM?
faq.answer: It introduces an agency sales pipeline using HubSpot or a suitable CRM.

faq.question: Will I learn ClickUp or Notion?
faq.answer: Yes. One accessible project-management platform is used for the core classroom workflow.

faq.question: What is an SOP?
faq.answer: A Standard Operating Procedure documents how a recurring task should be performed, checked and escalated.

faq.question: How many SOPs will I create?
faq.answer: Five core SOPs covering sales handoff, onboarding, delivery QA, changes and final reporting/handover.

faq.question: Will I learn contractor management?
faq.answer: Yes. You will prepare a role brief, paid sample assessment, evaluation rubric and onboarding/access checklist.

faq.question: Will I learn to acquire clients?
faq.answer: You will learn ethical acquisition channels, qualification and CRM management. The course does not guarantee clients or require live outreach.

faq.question: Will I learn AI agency automation?
faq.answer: You will learn responsible AI-assisted planning, documentation and operational review. Advanced autonomous systems are not mandatory.

faq.question: Will I learn GST and agency registration?
faq.answer: The course introduces India-specific business registration, GST, invoicing, contracts and data-protection awareness. It does not provide individualized legal or tax advice.

faq.question: Is Udyam registration mandatory for every student?
faq.answer: No. Students learn what the official process is and when it may be relevant. They are not required to register a business to pass the course.

faq.question: Can agencies work with international clients?
faq.answer: Yes, subject to service capability, contracts, banking, applicable tax and foreign-exchange requirements. The course introduces relevant considerations.

faq.question: Will this course guarantee a profitable agency?
faq.answer: No. The program teaches planning and operations; profitability depends on real demand, pricing, quality, cash flow, capacity and business decisions.

faq.question: What portfolio will I complete?
faq.answer: An Agency Operations Blueprint containing niche positioning, three packages, financial model, CRM pipeline, onboarding, five SOPs, contractor evaluation and a 90-day action plan.

faq.question: Are paid tools required?
faq.answer: Core exercises should use accessible tools or simulations. Paid CRM, project-management, automation or AI subscriptions are not mandatory.

faq.question: Is this different from Freelancing Mastery?
faq.answer: Yes. Freelancing Mastery focuses on independent professional service work, while this course concentrates on structured agency business and operational systems.

faq.question: Can I study without hiring contractors?
faq.answer: Yes. Contractor evaluation and team workflows are simulated.

faq.question: Is this an MBA or legal certification?
faq.answer: No. It is a focused practical agency operations certification.
